title: Miquel point of a triangle
statement: For D∈BC, E∈CA, F∈AB (or on the extended side-lines), prove that circumcircles (AEF), (BFD), (CDE) have a common point.
local_hints: Do not prove three-circle concurrency at once: create the common point from two circles first.
Recall GEO-MIQUEL-01 · Build a Miquel point from two circles.
Let M be the second intersection of (AEF) and (BFD). Rewrite two angles at M using cyclicity and test whether C,D,E,M are cyclic.
answer: The three circles meet at the Miquel point

title: Equal tangent segments and a bisected segment
statement: A circle has tangent segments AB at A and CD at C with AB=CD. Line BD meets AC at M. Prove AM=MC.
local_hints: Compare the two triangles cut by BD and AC at M; their M-angles are vertical.
Recall GEO-TRIG-01 · Use sine rule only when it shortens the geometry.

title: Two quarter-circle arcs inside a 4×2 rectangle
statement: In rectangle ABCD, AB=4 and BC=2. E,F are midpoints of AB,CD. Arc ESD is on the circle centred at A; arc ETC is on the circle centred at B. The perpendicular bisector of EF meets the arcs at S,T. Find ST.
local_hints: The perpendicular bisector of EF is a horizontal midline in a natural coordinate placement.
Recall GEO-COORD-01 · Place coordinates to remove constraints.

title: Centroid and the sum of squared sides
statement: P is the centroid of △ABC, with a=BC, b=CA, c=AB. Prove a²+b²+c²=3(PA²+PB²+PC²).
local_hints: Put the centroid at the origin so the three vertex vectors sum to zero.
Recall GEO-VECTOR-01 · Use vectors for centroids and parallelograms.

title: Perpendicular medians and two half-side lengths
statement: D,E are midpoints of AB,AC. Medians CD and BE meet at P with ∠BPC=90°. Given BD=8√5 and CE=6√5, find BC.
local_hints: Perpendicular medians become one dot-product equation after a good vector placement.
Recall GEO-COORD-01 · Place coordinates to remove constraints.

title: Reciprocal lengths in an isosceles triangle
statement: In isosceles △ABC, AB=AC=1. D,E are midpoints of AB,AC and P lies on DE. CP meets AB at F; BP meets AC at G. Find 1/BF+1/CG.
local_hints: Because P lies on the mid-segment DE, one parameter can describe the whole configuration.
Recall GEO-SIM-01 · Prove similarity before using ratios.
Parameterize P between D and E; find where CP and BP meet the opposite sides, and keep the parameter symbolic so it can cancel.

title: Cevian lengths determine the area
statement: P lies inside △ABC. A−P−D, B−P−E, C−P−F are cevians with D∈BC,E∈CA,F∈AB. AP=6, PD=6, BP=9, PE=3, CF=20. Find [ABC].
local_hints: The given cevian split ratios encode the relative areas of the three triangles around P.
Recall GEO-CEVA-01 · Use side ratios to test concurrency and area weights.
Convert AP:PD and BP:PE into area weights first; use those weights to recover the missing P-to-vertex length before any coordinate calculation.

title: Three perpendicularities in a quadrilateral
statement: In convex KLMN, MN⊥KM and KL⊥LN, with MN=65 and KL=28. The line through L perpendicular to KN meets KM at O. If KO=8, find MO.
local_hints: Several perpendicularities are a strong signal to choose coordinates.
Recall GEO-COORD-01 · Place coordinates to remove constraints.
Put KM on the x-axis with K=(0,0), O=(8,0), M=(m,0); encode each perpendicularity as a dot product.

title: Circumcenter and orthocenter angle identity
statement: Let O,H be the circumcenter and orthocenter of an acute △ABC. Prove ∠BAH=∠CAO.
local_hints: Both target angles can be rewritten using angle B.

title: Median determines the third side and area
statement: Two sides of a triangle are 10 cm and 5 cm. The median to the third side is 6.5 cm. If the area is 6√p cm², find p.
local_hints: The median should determine the missing third side before you compute area.
Recall GEO-MEDIAN-01 · Classify medians and use Apollonius.

title: Equal chords formed by extended medians
statement: In scalene △ABC, the medians from A,B,C meet the circumcircle again at L,M,N. If LM=LN, prove AB²+AC²=2BC².
local_hints: Translate LM=LN as equal-chord information before doing side algebra.
Use the equal chords to obtain the geometric symmetry relation first; only then rewrite the medians with Apollonius.

title: Two equal-length cuts on the hypotenuse
statement: In right △ABC with ∠ACB=90°, E,F lie on hypotenuse AB with AE=AC and BF=BC. Find ∠ECF.
local_hints: AE=AC and BF=BC create two isosceles triangles immediately.
Recall GEO-ISO-01 · Turn equal lengths into equal angles.

title: Four consecutive equal segments
statement: In △ADE, ∠ADE=140°. Points B∈AD and C∈AE satisfy AB=BC=CD=DE. Find ∠EAD.
local_hints: The four equal segments make a chain of overlapping isosceles triangles.
Recall GEO-ISO-01 · Turn equal lengths into equal angles.
Start from the 140° end: use CD=DE first, then BC=CD, then AB=BC, propagating equal base angles toward A.
